edits.new: The boy came up on Sunday at nine minutes past ten

edits.old: which was nine weeks to the day
edits.new: which was ten weeks to the day
edits.why: nine weeks from the night of 16/17 February is 21 April, the morning Elena interviews her father; the collision was invisible to a reader and only showed up on a calendar, so the withdrawal moves a week clear of it

edits.old: At twenty past nine he took his badge and went out to the corridor by the fire doors for air, which was what everybody did at that hour,
edits.new: At twenty past six he took his badge and went out to the corridor by the fire doors, which was what everybody did at the end of the shift,
edits.why: his queue closes at six and the rota runs after it; 21:20 was mine, not his

edits.old: He went back to his desk. There were one hundred and six records left. He closed all of them.
edits.new: He went back to his desk. The number at the bottom right of the screen said one hundred and six, and he had it to zero before the lights went down to half, and it did not occur to him until he was in the car park that she had not answered the question.
edits.why: closes the beat on the question rather than on the count, and does not pre-empt the interlude's later reflection

edits.old: and he did not write anything in the book that day, or for twenty-six days.
edits.new: and he did not write in the book again until the Monday, when he wrote three lines in a row and stopped telling himself it was a list.
edits.why: the interlude has thirty-one entries in the book nine days later; 'twenty-six days' made him stop writing, which contradicted it
